hypothesis: Switch II small-molecule drugs that work on KRAS G12C lose binding when pocket residues such as Y96 change; a designed miniprotein that uses a larger surface can keep contacts outside the sotorasib epitope and should be tested on Y96D, not only on wild-type G12C.

items.summary: Best fixture survivor: plausible fold confidence, mutant scores do not collapse, novelty not a PDB copy. Still only a computer result.
items.remaining_risk: No wet-lab binding. Fixture metrics. Must measure KD on G12C vs Y96D before anyone treats this as a drug lead.

items.summary: Looks acceptable on WT in the fixture and falls apart on Y96D. pLDDT is below the spec bar.
